newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - cash down, futures swoon.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - cash down, futures swoon.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds ended down 3/8 to 1/2 point, and more in spots, amid sharper losses in muni futures.
"The market's got a pretty heavy tone to it," a municipal trader said. "I think a lot of people are really perplexed about the municipal contract being down so much more than Treasuries here."

The September municipal contract closed down 1-3/32 at 117-8/32. The September T-bond contract closed down 12/32 at 112-5/32. The MOB spread was 163 ticks. In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was down 17/32 at 98-31/32 to yield 6.70 percent in late New York trade.

A second trader cited a "large seller in the (muni) contract today," who was long and decided to get out. The trader described the seller, whom he declined to name, as "a non-traditional municipal player who trades the contract."
"He just trades commodity futures, and muni futures are one of them," the trader said.
The first trader said muni futures' decline was contributing to weakness in muni cash, where action was thin.

"I don't know if they are waiting for new issues tomorrow or just letting the Street sort itself out," the trader said. "But boy, there's no one lifting their head to buy a bond, I can tell you that."

This week's new issues are expected to total $7 billion, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group. The tally includes $2.7 billion of taxable New Jersey Economic Development Authority debt via Merrill Lynch & Co.
"Supply is always a two-edged sword," a trader said. "It can be a wet blanket or it can be lighter fluid. It can ignite the market, but right now it feels like a wet blanket."
Over the past few months, municipal supply has been thin, he said.
"All of a sudden everybody has a little bit of paper, and there is some more coming," the trader said.
Tuesday's municipal bond sales are expected to total $2 billion in 49 sales, according to Reuters.
Negotiated offerings total $1.1 billion in 25 sales, with a $180 million Allegheny County Sanitary Authority, Pa., through Commonwealth Securities topping the list.
On the competitive side, 24 sales totaling $970 million are scheduled. A $300 million Massachusettes deal at 1000 EDT is the largest.
